deadline: Saturday before qualifying (exact time not specified)
central_unknown: Whether F1 Fantasy will retroactively apply Gasly's reinstated Monaco P3 points before the Barcelona deadline, which affects his price trajectory and the Gasly vs Hadjar decision for the B-tier/4A-light slot. Secondary uncertainty is McLaren's reliability — strong pace in FP2 but ongoing DNF concerns make them a risky constructor pick.

budget_tiers.core: Russell x2 or Antonelli x2, Mercedes, Ferrari, Hadjar

captains.label: Primary
captains.name: Kimi Antonelli
captains.reason: Won five GPs in a row, podium in every race, best car on the grid, massively underpriced at 2+ points per million. Universal consensus across all channels — absolute must-have and must-captain.

captains.label: Differential
captains.name: George Russell
captains.reason: P2 in FP2 with best first sector of anyone. Vegas betting lines have Mercedes 1-2 favored. Could be a bounceback race but unlikely to get Driver of the Day over Antonelli. ZachGP and FanAmp flag him as a differential.

captains.label: Differential
captains.name: Lewis Hamilton
captains.reason: Two consecutive P2 podiums, best driving since joining Ferrari. FormulaFantasyHub highlights him as a differential 2x option. Ferrari brought 8 upgrades including new front wing and floor.

buy.name: Liam Lawson
buy.note: Needs only -9 points for max 0.6M price rise. Double-digit points in 3 of last 4 races. 56% ownership in top 500. Long-term hold through Austria as well. Gearbox issue in FP2 is a reliability concern but still consensus top B-tier pick.

buy.name: Nico Hulkenberg
buy.note: Can only lose 0.2M max — effectively risk-free on budget. Universal consensus pick for budget building. Needs 8-9 points for max rise at corrected price. Cooling concerns at hot Barcelona track noted but negligible budget downside.

buy.name: Isack Hadjar
buy.note: Only needs 3 points for min price rise, 13 for max. In a top-4 car at Red Bull. Preferred over Gasly by F1FantasyPolePosition for long-term hold due to better forward price trajectory. Key piece of 4A-light builds.

consider.name: Pierre Gasly
consider.note: If Monaco P3 points are applied, could see a large 0.8M retroactive price increase making him a fantastic early pickup. Needs 4 points for min rise, 14 for max. Alpine bringing season-defining upgrade. FanAmp's top lineup features him. ZachGP says pick Gasly if points are applied, Hadjar if not.

consider.name: Franco Colapinto
consider.note: Only needs 1 point to avoid price fall, 9 for max rise. Most consistent B-tier driver per FanAmp. But F1FantasyPolePosition warns he's a short-term hold — likely needs transferring out after Barcelona when his Canada 25-pointer drops off.

consider.name: Gabriel Bortoleto
consider.note: Consistent 5-7 points recent races. Needs 6 to avoid fall, 11 for max rise. Audi bringing updates and had success at Barcelona in 2025. Cooling concerns flagged. Pairs well with Hulkenberg for double-Audi budget build.

consider.name: Arvid Lindblad
consider.note: Looked good in FP2 top 10. If he scores 8 points, his future price rise targets become very achievable. Racing Bulls reliability is a concern after Lawson's FP2 gearbox issue. Good long-term budget builder.

avoid: Lando Norris — strong pace (P1 FP2) but will lose ~0.3M in price regardless of result, needs 58+ points to rise which is virtually impossible. McLaren reliability concerns.
Oscar Piastri — McLaren reliability too risky for his price point. Two DNFs in recent races from the team.
Charles Leclerc — will lose price this week after Monaco DNF. Still expected to outscore Piastri but not worth 2x. FormulaFantasyHub keeps him in tier list but not as a buy.

chips.name: Limitless
chips.reason: Consensus to save — reliability issues are hitting every team making Limitless very risky. FanAmp and community suggest targeting Zandvoort after summer break (sprint weekend, reliability should be sorted). Joe Malazo comment endorsed by FanAmp.

chips.name: Wildcard
chips.reason: Multiple creators suggest saving wildcard for when 4A builds become affordable in 3-4 weeks. F1FantasyPolePosition prefers rolling transfers over using wildcard now.

chips.name: Final Fix
chips.reason: ReinFantasy argues saving for grid/engine penalties later. F1FantasyPolePosition acknowledges it can be used if qualifying reveals a clear swap (e.g., Antonelli to Leclerc or vice versa) but prefers saving.

watch_items: F1 Fantasy retroactive points correction for Gasly's Monaco P3 — confirmed won't happen before Barcelona deadline, but could trigger a 0.8M price increase post-race
McLaren vs Red Bull potential counter-appeals to the Monaco FIA ruling — could reverse Gasly's reinstatement entirely
Racing Bulls reliability — Lawson lost power/gearbox in FP2, team has 2 GP DNFs and 2 sprint DNFs this season
Ferrari's 8-component upgrade package (new front wing, new floor) — biggest upgrade of any team this weekend; could shift constructor pecking order
Alpine's season-defining upgrade package — could elevate Gasly and Colapinto's scoring potential
Audi cooling issues flagged in Barcelona heat (30°C+) — monitor FP3 before committing to double-Audi build
Hulkenberg price correction from 3.5M to 3.2M — F1 Fantasy must fix before deadline or strategy changes
Tires one step softer (C2/C3/C4 vs last year's C1/C2/C3) — could open multi-stop strategies and increase overtaking
arc: Barcelona is a pivotal budget-building race that sets up a crucial two-race stretch. The key strategic arc is transitioning toward 4A-light builds (two A-tier drivers + two A-tier constructors) over the next 3-4 weeks. Lawson and Hulkenberg are long-term holds through Austria (next race), while Colapinto is a one-week rental whose value drops when his Canada 25-pointer falls off the rolling average. The Gasly vs Hadjar decision may resolve after Barcelona when F1 Fantasy processes the Monaco correction — whoever gets the points boost becomes the preferred bridge to eventually affording a true 4A lineup (e.g., Antonelli + Leclerc + Mercedes + Ferrari). Austria follows immediately as a back-to-back, so rolling a transfer into that race is valuable. Silverstone (sprint weekend) comes three weeks later and could be a chip opportunity if reliability stabilizes.
